mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production by more than 2% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing output, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and related economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 5% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure and tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 5% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP increases and retail and food services sales also increase over the same quarter, it signals a broad-based economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of the instances where GDPC1 and RSAFS increased over the same quarter.
